    Two interval families on a finite-dimensional space #

    An interval family on a subspace V indexed by a linear order T is a choice of subspaces lo t ≤ hi t ≤ V with hi t ≤ lo t' for t < t', such that every nonzero vector of V lies in some hi t but not in lo t (Ringel's functorial filtrations give such families). For two families A, B the grid pieces are num t t' = A.hi t ⊓ B.hi t' modulo den t t' = A.lo t ⊓ B.hi t' ⊔ A.hi t ⊓ B.lo t'.

    • le_of_num_le: a subspace W with num ≤ W ⊔ den everywhere contains V.
    • finrank_eq_sum: dim V is the sum of the grid dimensions.
